Forecast of the raw series

Source: R/forecast.R
forecast.jd3_model.Rd

Forecasts the raw series from the pre-adjustment model (RegARIMA / TRAMO) of a model fitted with X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), REGARIMA() or TRAMO(). The values are read from the stored JDemetra+ result, so the seasonal adjustment itself is not affected. For the past, see backcast().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
forecast(object, new_data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted jd3_model (usually a column of a mable).

new_data

A tsibble of future dates, built by fabletools from the horizon h. It must start right after the end of the series.

...

Other arguments passed by forecast() (e.g. times), ignored.

Value

A distribution vector (see distributional) with one element per row of new_data: log-normal if the series is log-transformed, normal otherwise. Called through forecast() on a mable, the result is a fable.

Distribution

For log-transformed series, the forecast distribution is log-normal, with a median equal to JDemetra+'s forecast (a plain back-transformation of the forecast of the log). Its mean is therefore the bias-corrected forecast, and the difference grows with the horizon. For other series, the distribution is normal and its mean equals the median.

The default point forecast .mean of the resulting fable is the mean of the distribution. Use the point_forecast argument of forecast() to choose another summary, e.g. point_forecast = list(.median = median) to obtain JDemetra+'s forecast.

See also

backcast(), X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), jd3_indicator() to extract the raw indicators (y_f, y_ef...).

Examples

y  <- tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers)
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value))

# The mean is the bias-corrected forecast
forecast(mb, h = 12)
#> # A fable: 12 x 4 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#>    .model    index
#>    <chr>     <mth>
#>  1 x13    1961 Jan
#>  2 x13    1961 Feb
#>  3 x13    1961 Mar
#>  4 x13    1961 Apr
#>  5 x13    1961 May
#>  6 x13    1961 Jun
#>  7 x13    1961 Jul
#>  8 x13    1961 Aug
#>  9 x13    1961 Sep
#> 10 x13    1961 Oct
#> 11 x13    1961 Nov
#> 12 x13    1961 Dec
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: value <dist>, .mean <dbl>

# JDemetra+'s own forecast (median of the distribution)
forecast(mb, h = 12, point_forecast = list(.median = median))
#> # A fable: 12 x 4 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#>    .model    index
#>    <chr>     <mth>
#>  1 x13    1961 Jan
#>  2 x13    1961 Feb
#>  3 x13    1961 Mar
#>  4 x13    1961 Apr
#>  5 x13    1961 May
#>  6 x13    1961 Jun
#>  7 x13    1961 Jul
#>  8 x13    1961 Aug
#>  9 x13    1961 Sep
#> 10 x13    1961 Oct
#> 11 x13    1961 Nov
#> 12 x13    1961 Dec
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: value <dist>, .median <dbl>
